items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: And it happened to be that I was listening to Joe Oliver at that time. That was my introduction to it.

ctx.x: When did you first become aware that there was such a form of music as New Orleans?

Well, my introduction to it was many, many years ago. I don't think I was aware of it as being jazz, nor was it called jazz then, but I had a nice, a Negro nice, who used to take me walking up and down St. Charles Avenue, and occasionally, a mother would let me accompany her to the grocery, which was in the Negro section about five squares away from St. Charles Avenue towards Dryad Street. And it was amazing how she seemed to get by grapevine that every time we went to this grocery, there'd always be a funeral…
Well, what did your parents think of this whole music? And your parents...
